population_scope: US all-type house transactions, Massachusetts 1987-2008 (1.78M sales; Warren Group), reference distance 0.05 miles
notes: queue-18 LANDED v1.22: forced-sale price spillover. POINT is the authors' PREFERRED estimate: each foreclosure ~0.05 miles away lowers the price of a house by about 1% (lead-vs-lag difference-in-difference in the Leigh-Rockoff style: foreclosures within 0.1mi before the sale vs within 0.1mi after, inner-circle 0.1mi vs outer-ring 0.25mi; zero distance -2%, 0.05mi -1%). Stored as a gap multiplier: 1 - 0.01 = 0.99. BAND: the preferred DiD reports NO standard error, so the band is the rounding band (point +/-25%, CITING section 3 rule 3 phrasing) with the SE-carrying hedonic associates recorded beside, NOT averaged in: per foreclosure within 0.25mi year-before-sale -1.8% (col 1), -1.1% controlling recent neighborhood unforced prices (col 2); 0.1mi distance-weighted at zero distance -9.1% (col 1) / -7.3% (col 2) - clustering-inflated per the authors' own diagnosis, recorded to bound the same-location tail (their 99.9th-percentile dummies reach -21% to -26%). PERSISTENCE (Table 14): lagged foreclosures keep comparable coefficients a year out - spillovers are not transitory liquidity discounts. HETEROGENEITY (Table 13): larger for single-family and condos, absent for multifamily; larger for cheap houses in cheap zipcodes (vandalism mechanism). AGGREGATE (their 2008Q1 calculation): typical foreclosure cost $46,000 on the foreclosed house + $406,000 total on neighbors (col-2 model) or $110,000 (DiD). IDENTIFICATION LIMIT (authors' own statement): no instrument found; estimates are NOT structural - timing (lead vs lag) and distance gradient are the only quasi-experimental handles, so this lands as a PARALLEL-STREAM boundary-applied level response, never composed into the earnings/child chains (housing-contagion composition is a queued P3 item). CLASS/VERSION CAVEAT: read via NBER w14866 (April 2009 pre-publication draft); the published AER 2011 abstract confirms the preferred estimate (about 1% at 0.05mi) and the 27% foreclosure discount - table-level numbers are the WP's, tier therefore EXACT-results not EXACT.
